items.title: Why Lebanon's displaced residents say this war with Israel is different
items.description: Southern Lebanon has a "very long history" of conflict with Israel, and many of its residents remember past wars clearly. But they say the latest incursion feels different.

items.title: Israel says it has killed Iran's navy commander, Trump says Tehran 'begging' for a deal
items.description: Israel's Defence Minister Israel Katz says an Israeli air strike has killed the commander of the Iranian Revolutionary Guards' navy.

items.title: States to seek consistent reporting of fuel shortages at national cabinet
items.description: State and territory leaders are also expected to push for a national approach to any further measures, including fuel rationing, if supply were to run short.

items.title: A new 'kangaroo route?' Qantas shifts strategy as Middle East routes collapse
items.description: Qantas will increase capacity on flights between Australia and Europe after Easter, which experts say may see the "kangaroo route" evolve.

items.title: Fuel dominates politics, Hanson questioned over flights
items.description: The ongoing fuel crisis dominated politics this week but a probe into the National Anti-Corruption Commission was also announced and Pauline Hanson was grilled about accepting free flights from Gina Rinehart.

items.title: How a landmark social media ruling could influence thousands of other cases
items.description: A US jury has found Instagram and YouTube were designed to be addictive to young users, in a landmark trial experts say could influence thousands of similar lawsuits.

items.title: WA coast 'pummelled' as Cyclone Narelle could reach category five on approach
items.description: Authorities in Western Australia say they are preparing for weather not seen since 2021, when a deadly cyclone flattened buildings in a town unaccustomed to such extreme conditions.

items.title: Last-touch non-call labelled 'farce' as Geelong edges Adelaide in thriller
items.description: Geelong continues its streak over Adelaide at Kardinia Park, as one of the AFL's off-season rule changes is put squarely in the spotlight for the wrong reasons.

items.title: Cherry-Evans has last laugh as Sea Eagles slump to third-straight defeat
items.description: Daly Cherry-Evans is roundly booed on his return to Brookvale after his off-season switch from the Sea Eagles to the Roosters, as the tricolours dominate territory to claim 33-16 victory.

items.title: Fuel costs drive COVID-like surge in demand for emergency relief
items.description: Rising petrol and diesel prices are driving Canberra families to seek emergency assistance and forcing small businesses to consider whether to pass on higher costs to customers.

items.title: Drug-fuelled driver who hit schoolboys sues Commonwealth over arrest
items.description: Tayler Hazell, who will be sentenced tomorrow over a hit-and-run that seriously injured two children, is suing the federal government, alleging police violently treated him during his arrest.

items.title: The One Nation vote in SA
items.description: One Nation just sent a shiver through the Liberal Party, after a breakthrough result in South Australia.  Pauline Hanson's party achieved more than 21 per cent of the statewide primary vote, beating the Liberal Party and becoming the second-highest polling party. But nationally, more attention has been on the undercard fight, and that has left the Liberal Party deeply wounded.

items.title: Severe storm causes 11,000 power outages, knocks out transport
items.description: Fire and Rescue NSW says there has been more than 400 calls for help, including one incident where a tree fell on a house trapping the occupant.

items.title: Man who allegedly lured actors into sex acts handed 45 more charges
items.description: Police have laid 45 more charges dating back to 2014 against a Sydney man accused of posing as a Disney casting agent and offering movie opportunities for sex acts, with a magistrate describing it as "some of the most manipulative behaviour I've seen".

items.title: Here's who you should see at comedy festivals across Australia
items.description: Comedy season is in full swing, with festivals across the country hosting the best acts from Australia and the world. We asked our favourites to share their recommendations.

items.title: Music for reflection across Holy Week, Passover and Easter
items.description: Your guide to listening for music of reflection and rejuvenation on ABC Classic across Holy Week, Passover and Easter.

items.title: What should you eat to keep your brain sharp as you get older?
items.description: The food choices we make over decades — not just in later life, but across adulthood — may quietly shape the health of our brains in ways that only become visible much later.

items.title: AFL concussion class action expands to more than 100 former players
items.description: Eight more footballers have joined a multimillion-dollar concussion class action against the AFL, tipping the total to over 100 former players who all claim they have been left brain-damaged by the game.

items.title: Lift minimum wage above the rate of inflation, federal government urges
items.description: In its submission to the Fair Work Commission's annual wage review, the government again calls for the lowest-paid workers to not go backwards.

items.title: Vegetable growers won't plant more crops if costs keep rising
items.description: A snap survey by AUSVEG reveals 27 per cent of Australian vegetable growers have already reduced planting, while some will not harvest current crops because rising costs make it unviable.

items.title: TGA proposes removing sunscreen SPF numbers in regulation changes
items.description: The proposals include a number of changes to SPF testing requirements, oversight of the labs that do SPF testing, and the way SPF is labelled — reforms that would overhaul the sunscreen industry.

items.title: Gold Coast mayor yet to decide if he'll vote on Trump tower after gifts
items.description: Tom Tate has been pressed on whether he would exclude himself from chambers if the Trump tower came to a vote, after he received gifts from the organisation.

items.title: Discerning crocs from logs the challenge for AI trial
items.description: Researchers are trialling artificial intelligence to detect crocodiles in north Queensland waterways, but its success depends on human training to ensure accuracy.

items.title: Katherine escapes more flood damage as remote evacuees start heading home
items.description: Major flooding has eased along the Katherine River and the town has been spared further damage, while surrounding remote communities are starting to recover.

items.title: Video captures dramatic moment crane collapses in powerful storm
items.description: Emergency evacuations are underway after a crane collapses in a powerful storm in western NSW.
